topic: Tuberculosis treatment in renal impairment and hemodialysis
core_rules: Always retrieve creatinine clearance/eGFR, dialysis status, weight, age, regimen and exact medicine before giving dose-specific information.
Do not reduce milligram dose indiscriminately; for several anti-TB drugs, guidance changes dosing interval rather than simply lowering each dose.
For hemodialysis, timing relative to dialysis matters and must be retrieved from current guidance.
Coordinate management with nephrology/TB specialists for severe renal impairment or dialysis.
Do not extrapolate dosing between levofloxacin and moxifloxacin; renal adjustment requirements differ.
Do not assume all renal dysfunction is caused by TB drugs; review baseline CKD, dehydration, sepsis and other nephrotoxins.

who_ds_tb_crcl_lt_30.pyrazinamide: 25–35 mg/kg per dose, three times weekly after dialysis
who_ds_tb_crcl_lt_30.ethambutol: 15–25 mg/kg per dose, three times weekly after dialysis
who_ds_tb_crcl_lt_30.moxifloxacin: WHO states no renal dose adjustment is required in this DS-TB context
who_ds_tb_crcl_lt_30.rifapentine: WHO states no renal dose adjustment is required in this DS-TB context

levofloxacin.note: WHO DR-TB guidance requires renal dose adjustment when creatinine clearance is reduced; exact threshold depends on regimen/guidance context and must be retrieved.

monitoring.creatinine: WHO recommends close monitoring, often weekly or every 2 weeks in chronic renal failure.
monitoring.electrolytes: Weekly monitoring is recommended in CRF because electrolyte disturbances are frequent.
monitoring.ECG: Consider because electrolyte abnormalities and QT-prolonging drugs may coexist.

dialysis.general: Several anti-TB medicines are preferentially administered after hemodialysis; exact drug-specific schedule must be retrieved.
dialysis.foundational_pk: Older PK data show pyrazinamide is substantially dialyzed; retained as background evidence only.
